_comment: Initial Windows 11 audit rule set. See FRAMEWORK.md for the rationale behind each category/check and for the operator vocabulary used in expected_condition. Rule field_path values are relative to the named collector's CollectionResult.data.

rules.description: Report the installed Windows edition/caption.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the Windows build number.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the OS architecture (x64/ARM64).
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the host name and domain/workgroup membership.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the processor model and core count.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report total installed physical memory.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report fixed storage volumes and free space.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report whether the system boots via UEFI or legacy BIOS.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Secure Boot should be enabled to prevent unauthorized boot-time code from running.
rules.remediation: Enable Secure Boot in UEFI firmware settings.

rules.description: A present, enabled, and initialized TPM is required for BitLocker and modern platform security features.
rules.remediation: Ensure a TPM 2.0 chip is present, enabled in firmware, and initialized.

rules.description: Report time since last boot.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the system's primary IPv4 address (the interface with a default gateway).
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the MAC address of the system's primary network adapter (the interface with a default gateway).
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the system's hardware serial number, as recorded in firmware.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the system's BIOS/firmware version.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the path Windows is installed into.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the path to the Windows system directory (System32).
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the system's processor architecture identifier (e.g. AMD64, ARM64).
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the active network connection's profile name and status.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the name of the system's primary network interface (the interface with a default gateway).
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the name of the wireless (802.11) network interface, if one is present.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the date Windows was originally installed on this system.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the domain (or workgroup) this system is joined to.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: The operating system should be Windows 10 or Windows 11; earlier or unsupported Windows versions no longer receive security updates.
rules.remediation: Upgrade this system to a supported Windows version (Windows 10 or Windows 11); unsupported Windows versions no longer receive security updates.

rules.description: Report the installed Windows service pack, if any.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the installed Windows product ID.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the Windows activation/license status.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report all local user accounts.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: The built-in Guest account should be disabled to prevent anonymous local access.
rules.remediation: Disable the built-in Guest account via Local Users and Groups.

rules.description: No local account should be configured to allow a blank password.
rules.data_source: Local Security Accounts Manager (SAM), PasswordRequired flag
rules.remediation: Require a password for every local account; clear the PasswordNotRequired flag.

rules.description: The local Administrators group should contain only the accounts that genuinely need administrative rights.
rules.remediation: Review membership of the local Administrators group; remove accounts that do not need administrative rights.

rules.description: Local accounts unused for a long period should be disabled or removed.
rules.data_source: Local Security Accounts Manager (SAM), LastLogon property
rules.remediation: Disable or remove local accounts that have not logged on in the last 90 days.

rules.description: The built-in Administrator account (well-known SID suffix -500) should be disabled in favor of a named administrative account.
rules.remediation: Disable the built-in Administrator account and use a named administrative account instead.

rules.description: Passwords should meet a minimum length to resist brute-force and guessing attacks.
rules.data_source: Local Security Policy, System Access section
rules.remediation: Set minimum password length to at least 8 characters via Local Security Policy > Account Policies > Password Policy.

rules.description: Password complexity requirements reduce the risk of trivially guessable passwords.
rules.data_source: Local Security Policy, System Access section
rules.remediation: Enable the 'Password must meet complexity requirements' policy.

rules.description: Passwords should expire periodically, but not be set to never expire.
rules.data_source: Local Security Policy, System Access section
rules.remediation: Set a maximum password age between 1 and 365 days (a value of 0 means passwords never expire, which is not recommended).

rules.description: Preventing password reuse reduces the effectiveness of credential replay.
rules.data_source: Local Security Policy, System Access section
rules.remediation: Remember at least 5 previous passwords to prevent reuse.

rules.description: Locking accounts after a small number of failed attempts slows brute-force attacks.
rules.data_source: Local Security Policy, System Access section
rules.remediation: Set account lockout threshold between 1 and 10 invalid attempts (0 disables lockout entirely, which is not recommended).

rules.description: Locked accounts should remain locked long enough to blunt automated retry attacks.
rules.data_source: Local Security Policy, System Access section
rules.remediation: Set account lockout duration to at least 15 minutes.

rules.description: UAC is a core defense against unauthorized privilege escalation and should never be disabled.
rules.remediation: Enable UAC (EnableLUA) via Local Security Policy or registry.

rules.parameter: UAC Consent Prompt Behavior for Administrators
rules.description: Administrators should be prompted for consent on the secure desktop before elevation.
rules.remediation: Set UAC administrator consent behavior to 2 ('Prompt for consent on the secure desktop') or the Windows 11 out-of-box default of 5 ('Prompt for consent for non-Windows binaries on the secure desktop'); values 0 (elevate without prompting), 1, 3, and 4 skip the secure desktop or skip prompting entirely and are not recommended.

rules.description: The workstation should automatically lock after a period of inactivity to prevent unauthorized physical access when left unattended. Checked via the machine-wide 'Interactive logon: Machine inactivity limit' policy first (always enforces a password-protected lock when set), falling back to a password-protected screen saver (an active-but-insecure screen saver does not count, since it does not require a password on resume).
rules.data_source: Registry HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\InactivityTimeoutSecs, falling back to HKCU\Control Panel\Desktop (ScreenSaveActive, ScreenSaverIsSecure, ScreenSaveTimeOut)
rules.remediation: Configure an automatic screen lock: set the 'Interactive logon: Machine inactivity limit' policy, or enable a password-protected screen saver (Settings > Personalization > Lock screen > Screen saver settings, with 'On resume, display logon screen' checked).

rules.description: When an automatic lock is configured, a short inactivity timeout limits how long an unattended, unlocked session is exposed.
rules.data_source: Registry HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\InactivityTimeoutSecs, falling back to HKCU\Control Panel\Desktop\ScreenSaveTimeOut
rules.remediation: Set the inactivity lock timeout to 15 minutes or less.

rules.description: The antivirus engine itself should be active (unless a third-party AV is legitimately in control).
rules.remediation: Enable Microsoft Defender Antivirus, or confirm an authorized third-party antivirus is active in its place.

rules.description: Report the timestamp of the most recent Defender security intelligence (signature) update.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Net Protector's real-time protection service (ZeroVProtect) should be running. Reported NOT_APPLICABLE if Net Protector is not installed on this system.
rules.remediation: Start the Net Protector antivirus service, or reinstall Net Protector if the service is missing.

rules.description: Report the timestamp Windows Security Center last recorded for Net Protector's status/definitions. Reported NOT_APPLICABLE if Net Protector is not installed on this system.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: SmartScreen helps block known malicious apps and files. Checked via per-user (HKCU Explorer) and policy (HKLM) registry overrides; if neither is present, Windows does not persist this setting anywhere until changed from default (confirmed live), so absence is reported as Microsoft's documented on-by-default state rather than as unverifiable.
rules.data_source: Registry HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\SmartScreenEnabled, falling back to HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System\EnableSmartScreen, falling back to Microsoft's documented default (on) when neither override exists
rules.remediation: Enable Windows SmartScreen for apps and files.

rules.description: Report all antivirus products registered with Windows Security Center. This is informational: Security Center's productState value is an undocumented bitmask, so this tool lists registered product names for the reviewer's own judgment rather than decoding an unofficial encoding into a pass/fail claim. On systems with an active third-party antivirus, Microsoft Defender is expected to appear passive/stopped in the checks above by design — this list gives that context.
rules.remediation: Informational only; if a third-party product is listed, verify it is authorized and properly licensed, and that Defender's passive state is therefore expected.

rules.description: Windows Firewall should be enabled on the Domain profile.
rules.remediation: Enable Windows Firewall on the Domain profile.

rules.description: Windows Firewall should be enabled on the Private profile.
rules.remediation: Enable Windows Firewall on the Private profile.

rules.description: Windows Firewall should be enabled on the Public profile, which faces the least trusted networks.
rules.remediation: Enable Windows Firewall on the Public profile.

rules.description: Legacy, unencrypted, or commonly abused services (e.g. Telnet 23, FTP 21) should not be listening.
rules.remediation: Disable services listening on high-risk ports (e.g. Telnet 23, FTP 21) unless explicitly required.

rules.description: Report each network adapter's connection category (Public/Private/Domain).
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report configured DNS servers for each adapter.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: An unexpected proxy configuration can indicate unauthorized traffic interception.
rules.remediation: Verify any configured proxy is expected and authorized; an unexpected proxy can indicate traffic interception.

rules.description: Disabling wireless (Wi-Fi) network adapters when not needed reduces network attack surface, particularly on systems that should only connect via wired/managed networks. Advisory: only meaningful when a wireless adapter is present, and many systems legitimately need Wi-Fi.
rules.remediation: Disable the wireless network adapter (Settings > Network & internet > Wi-Fi, or Device Manager) if wired/managed connectivity is available and Wi-Fi is not required.

rules.description: Report currently established TCP connections (local/remote endpoint and owning process).
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report active UDP listening endpoints.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report every listening TCP port and its owning process, not just the high-risk subset scored by NET-004.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: A large number of simultaneous established TCP connections can indicate unexpected network activity (e.g. malware, unauthorized services) on an ordinary client workstation. Fails when the count exceeds 5.
rules.remediation: Review established TCP connections and their owning processes; investigate any that are unexpected.

rules.description: A large number of active UDP endpoints can indicate unexpected network activity (e.g. malware, unauthorized services) on an ordinary client workstation. Fails when the count exceeds 15.
rules.remediation: Review active UDP endpoints and their owning processes; investigate any that are unexpected.

rules.description: A large number of open (listening) TCP ports increases network attack surface on an ordinary client workstation. Fails when the count exceeds 6.
rules.data_source: Derived from listening_ports (distinct listening TCP port count)
rules.collection_method: Count of distinct ports in listening_ports
rules.remediation: Review listening TCP ports and their owning processes; close/disable services that are not required.

rules.description: The Windows Update service must be running for updates to be installed.
rules.remediation: Start and enable the Windows Update service (wuauserv).

rules.description: A system that has not received updates recently may be missing important security patches. This checks installed-update recency as a local, offline-safe proxy; it does not query Microsoft's update catalog for pending updates (see FRAMEWORK.md).
rules.remediation: Install pending security updates; system has not been updated recently.

rules.description: Windows Update should not be left paused indefinitely, which silently stops patch installation. Checked via the Group Policy NoAutoUpdate override (hard disable) and, more relevantly on a modern consumer install, the PauseUpdatesExpiryTime value written by Settings > Windows Update > Pause updates. Confirmed live via direct registry access that this value is genuinely absent (not merely unset/null) when updates are not paused, making its presence a definite, current signal rather than a guess.
rules.remediation: Resume Windows Update (Settings > Windows Update), or ensure updates are managed by an equivalent patch process.

rules.description: Report the date of the most recently installed update.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: The Windows Defender Firewall service (mpssvc) must be running for firewall rules to be enforced.
rules.remediation: Start the Windows Defender Firewall service (mpssvc) and set it to automatic startup.

rules.description: The Windows Defender Antivirus service (WinDefend) must be running to enforce Defender's protections.
rules.remediation: Start the Windows Defender Antivirus service (WinDefend).

rules.description: The Remote Registry service allows remote editing of the registry and should be disabled unless centrally required.
rules.remediation: Disable the Remote Registry service unless centrally required.

rules.description: The Print Spooler service has a history of privilege-escalation vulnerabilities (e.g. PrintNightmare); disable it on systems that do not print.
rules.remediation: Disable the Print Spooler service on systems that do not need printing.

rules.description: Report all services configured to start automatically.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report installed applications, sourced from registry Uninstall keys (Win32_Product is intentionally avoided; querying it can trigger MSI consistency-check side effects, which conflicts with the read-only requirement).
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: A very large number of auto-starting programs increases attack surface and often indicates unmanaged software sprawl.
rules.remediation: Review startup applications; remove unnecessary auto-starting programs.

rules.description: Report currently running processes.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Processes executing from temporary or user-writable directories (e.g. %TEMP%, %APPDATA%) can indicate malware.
rules.collection_method: PowerShell Get-Process, path heuristic against known-writable directories
rules.remediation: Investigate processes running from temporary or user-writable directories.

rules.description: Report installed software commonly flagged for review: unmanaged remote-access clients (TeamViewer, AnyDesk), virtualization software (VMware, VirtualBox), and registry/system cleaner utilities. Informational: presence alone isn't a universal fail (e.g. VMware/VirtualBox are legitimate developer tools).
rules.remediation: Review flagged software; uninstall anything not explicitly authorized for this system.

rules.description: Report every individually-registered MSI product/component on this system. Lower-level and noisier than the Installed Applications Inventory (APP-001) -- includes granular sub-packages (e.g. individual Visual Studio components) that never get a user-facing Uninstall entry.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: A very large number of installed programs increases attack surface and often indicates unmanaged software sprawl. Fails when the count exceeds 20.
rules.remediation: Review installed programs; uninstall software that is not required for this system's role.

rules.description: Remote Desktop increases remote attack surface and should be disabled unless required.
rules.remediation: Disable Remote Desktop unless required; if required, restrict access via firewall/VPN and enforce NLA.

rules.description: When RDP is enabled, Network Level Authentication should be required to authenticate before a session is established.
rules.remediation: Require Network Level Authentication (NLA) for RDP connections.

rules.description: Remote Assistance should be disabled unless actively required for support sessions.
rules.remediation: Disable Remote Assistance unless actively required for support.

rules.description: WinRM (remote management) should only be running when intentionally used, and restricted to trusted management hosts.
rules.remediation: Confirm WinRM is intentionally enabled and restricted to trusted management hosts.

rules.description: Unrestricted or Bypass execution policy removes a layer of protection against running untrusted scripts. The 'Process' scope is deliberately excluded from this check: this auditor invokes PowerShell with -ExecutionPolicy Bypass for its own commands, which would otherwise always show as a false 'Bypass' at Process scope regardless of the system's real persistent policy.
rules.data_source: PowerShell execution policy scope chain (MachinePolicy, UserPolicy, CurrentUser, LocalMachine scopes only)
rules.remediation: Set PowerShell execution policy to RemoteSigned or AllSigned instead of Unrestricted/Bypass.

rules.description: Script block logging improves the ability to detect and investigate malicious PowerShell use.
rules.remediation: Enable PowerShell Script Block Logging for improved auditability.

rules.description: Restricting installation of unauthorized device classes reduces risk from rogue peripherals.
rules.remediation: Consider enabling device installation restriction policy to control removable/peripheral hardware.

rules.description: The operating system drive should be encrypted to protect data at rest if the device is lost or stolen.
rules.remediation: Enable BitLocker on the operating system drive.

rules.description: All fixed data drives should be encrypted, not only the OS drive.
rules.data_source: BitLocker Drive Encryption status, all fixed volumes
rules.remediation: Enable BitLocker on all fixed data drives.

rules.description: Removable drives containing sensitive data should be encrypted with BitLocker To Go; this is reported as advisory since not all removable media holds sensitive data.
rules.data_source: BitLocker Drive Encryption status, removable volumes
rules.remediation: Consider enabling BitLocker To Go on removable drives that contain sensitive data.

rules.description: Unnecessary SMB shares expand the network attack surface.
rules.collection_method: PowerShell Get-SmbShare, excluding built-in administrative shares
rules.remediation: Review and remove unnecessary SMB shares; ensure remaining shares use least-privilege permissions.

rules.parameter: Unexpected Write Access on System Directories
rules.description: Non-administrative accounts should not have write access to core system directories.
rules.data_source: NTFS ACLs on C:\Windows and C:\Program Files
rules.remediation: Review NTFS permissions on system directories; non-administrative accounts should not have write access.

rules.description: Report folders shared with other systems (excluding built-in administrative shares).
rules.collection_method: PowerShell Get-SmbShare, excluding built-in administrative shares
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: A large number of shared folders expands the network attack surface and increases exposure of local data to other systems. Fails when the count exceeds 3.
rules.remediation: Review shared folders; remove any that are not explicitly required, and ensure remaining shares use least-privilege permissions.

rules.description: An undersized Security log rolls over quickly, losing evidence needed for incident investigation. Confirmed on a live Windows 11 system that even listing this log's metadata (not just reading entries) is denied without elevation.
rules.remediation: Increase the maximum size of the Security event log to reduce the risk of early log rollover.

rules.description: A high number of failed logon attempts in a short window can indicate brute-force activity.
rules.remediation: Investigate repeated failed logon attempts (possible brute-force activity).

rules.description: Without logon auditing enabled, authentication activity cannot be reconstructed after an incident.
rules.remediation: Enable auditing of logon events via auditpol.

rules.description: The System event log should be accessible for diagnosing system-level issues and changes.
rules.remediation: Ensure the System event log service is running and the log is accessible.

rules.description: Report whether USB mass-storage device installation is restricted. Reported informationally: whether restriction is appropriate is organization-specific.
rules.remediation: Informational only; review against your organization's device-control policy.

rules.description: Report currently attached USB devices.
rules.data_source: Plug and Play device tree, USB class
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report whether a Bluetooth adapter is present and its state.
rules.data_source: Plug and Play device tree, Bluetooth class
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the system-level camera privacy access setting.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report the system-level microphone privacy access setting.
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Disabling the Bluetooth radio when not needed reduces wireless attack surface. Advisory: only evaluated when a Bluetooth adapter is present, and many systems legitimately need Bluetooth for peripherals.
rules.data_source: Plug and Play device tree, Bluetooth class
rules.remediation: Disable the Bluetooth radio (Settings > Bluetooth & devices) if it is not actively required.

rules.description: An attached USB mass-storage device is a data exfiltration and malware-introduction vector. Advisory: legitimate use (backups, transfers) is common, so this is a warning rather than a hard fail.
rules.data_source: Plug and Play device tree, USB class (mass-storage entries)
rules.remediation: Disconnect any USB storage device not explicitly authorized for this system, per your organization's removable-media policy.

rules.description: Whether apps are permitted to access the camera. Advisory: many systems legitimately need camera access (video calls), so this is a warning rather than a hard fail.
rules.remediation: Deny camera access (Settings > Privacy & security > Camera) unless it is actively required.

rules.description: Whether apps are permitted to access the microphone. Advisory: many systems legitimately need microphone access (calls, dictation), so this is a warning rather than a hard fail.
rules.remediation: Deny microphone access (Settings > Privacy & security > Microphone) unless it is actively required.

rules.description: Report USB mass-storage devices ever connected to this system (not just currently attached), with serial number, manufacturer, and first/last-used dates.
rules.data_source: Plug and Play device tree, USBSTOR instances (including previously-removed devices)
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: Report installed browsers and their versions. Reported informationally only: this offline tool cannot check versions against the latest published release, so it does not assert up-to-date/outdated status (see FRAMEWORK.md limitations).
rules.data_source: Registry App Paths / Uninstall keys, executable file version info
rules.remediation: Informational only.

rules.description: SmartScreen in Microsoft Edge helps block malicious sites and downloads. Checked via the Edge policy registry override; if no policy is present, Edge does not persist this setting anywhere until changed from default (confirmed live, including a search of Edge's own Preferences JSON), so absence is reported as Microsoft's documented on-by-default state.
rules.data_source: Registry HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge\SmartScreenEnabled, falling back to Microsoft's documented default (on) when no policy override exists
rules.remediation: Enable SmartScreen for Microsoft Edge.

rules.description: An unexpected browser-level proxy override can indicate traffic interception.
rules.remediation: Verify any browser-level proxy override is expected and authorized.

rules.description: System Restore provides a rollback path after unwanted system changes. Checked via the DisableSR Group Policy override (hard disable, no elevation needed) and, when no policy is present, Get-ComputerRestorePoint: confirmed live that this cmdlet requires elevation and is documented to throw "System Restore is disabled on this computer" when protection is off system-wide, succeeding otherwise (even with zero existing restore points).
rules.data_source: Registry HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\SystemRestore\DisableSR, falling back to PowerShell Get-ComputerRestorePoint
rules.collection_method: winreg read, falling back to Get-ComputerRestorePoint success/failure
rules.remediation: Enable System Restore on the operating system drive.

rules.description: Report the state of the Windows Backup service (SDRSVC). Reported informationally: presence of the service does not confirm an actual backup job exists.
rules.remediation: Informational only; verify backups independently through your organization's backup solution.

rules.description: A Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) partition supports system repair and recovery.
rules.remediation: Ensure a Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) partition is present for system recovery.
